sections.html:
Post Falls is a Kootenai County city on the Rathdrum Prairie, right on the Washington border and about 20 miles east of Spokane. Coeur d'Alene borders it to the east, the town of Stateline and the state of Washington lie to the west, and the Spokane River forms its southern edge.

The city's elevation is 2,182 feet, and the Census Bureau counts about 15 square miles of land. The Census estimate for July 1, 2025 was 46,715 residents, up 21.0 percent from the April 2020 base of 38,620.

The city is named for Frederick Post, a German immigrant who built a lumber mill on the Spokane River in 1871. He bought the land from Andrew Seltice, chief of the Coeur d'Alene Tribe, and a pictograph on a granite cliff at Treaty Rock Park records the purchase.

Kootenai County has traditionally had a timber based economy, and that has been changing as the manufacturing base widens. The nearby lakes, rivers and mountains have also helped Post Falls develop tourism and retirement communities.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Post Falls housing?
sections.html:
Post Falls has the highest median home value of the four Idaho cities in this series, at $477,400 for owner-occupied units in the 2020 to 2024 survey. It also has the highest median household income, at $82,183.

About 87 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, the highest share among the four cities, so people who move here tend to stay put. A median value is a citywide estimate, so it says little about any single house. Source: Census Bureau QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Post Falls, and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Post Falls has four distinct seasons and a warm summer Mediterranean climate, with a lot of snow. The yearly average is about 59.3 inches of snowfall and 25.73 inches of total precipitation, with December and January the snowiest months at about 17 to 19 inches each.

Temperatures run from a record low of minus 30 degrees to a record high of 109. Average January highs sit in the mid 30s, and July highs reach the low 80s.

  • Roofs carry snow load for months, so buyers look closely at the age and slope of the roof.
  • Gutters, downspouts and drainage matter at spring thaw, when snowmelt can reach crawl spaces.
  • Heating systems and insulation draw questions in a city that averages more than 59 inches of snow.

If you have deferred any of this, an as-is sale lets you pass the work to the buyer instead of paying for it before you list.

sections.h2: What are the main employers and roads in Post Falls?
sections.html:
Education, health care and manufacturing provide most of the large jobs in the city. The 2022 city financial report lists the Post Falls School District as the largest employer, with 700 to 799 employees.

  • Health care: Pleasant View Surgery Center, Rehabilitation Hospital of the Northwest and North Idaho Day Surgery, each with 200 to 299 employees.
  • Manufacturing: Buck Knives with 200 to 299 and Tedder Industries with 150 to 199.
  • Public and retail: the City of Post Falls and Walmart, each with 200 to 299.

Interstate 90 runs through the city, linking Spokane to the west with Coeur d'Alene to the east. Idaho 41 meets the interstate east of town and runs 8 miles north to Rathdrum, and US 95 lies about 7 miles east. Spokane International Airport serves air travelers, and Amtrak stops in Spokane and Sandpoint. The mean commute time is 24.1 minutes.

Public schools in the city belong to the Post Falls School District 273. Its schools include Post Falls Middle School and the elementary schools Greensferry, Mullan Trail, Ponderosa, Prairie View, Seltice, Treaty Rock and West Ridge, plus Frederick Post Kindergarten.

Private options include Classical Christian Academy and Genesis Prep Academy. Buyers with children often ask which elementary school feeds a given address, so have the district's boundary information ready if you can.

sections.h2: How are Kootenai County property taxes collected?
sections.html:
Kootenai County says that under Idaho Code section 63-903 all property taxes are due in full on December 20 of the year they are levied, though real property owners may pay in two halves. The second half is due June 20.

Assessment notices go out at the end of May, and the county has about 45 taxing districts plus several special districts that share in your bill. The deadline for a Board of Equalization appeal is the fourth Monday of June. The treasurer's page says the property tax bill for the current cycle arrives in the first week of December.

  • Pay by mail only with a USPS postmark on or before the due date, since only those payments count as on time.
  • If you cannot pay, you may apply to the Board of County Commissioners for financial hardship relief at (208) 446-1600.
  • When real property is three years delinquent, the parcel enters the tax deed process, and the owner must pay the third year in full to stop it.

The tax deed rule matters for sellers who have fallen behind. See the Kootenai County Treasurer FAQ and the property tax process page.

sections.h2: What permits and disclosures apply to a Post Falls seller?
sections.html:
The City of Post Falls issues building permits for construction and renovation, and its Building page explains the process and codes. A change of use or occupancy needs its own permit, which matters if a house was ever used as an office or a rental.

The state's disclosure rule applies on top of that. Idaho Code section 55-2501 and the sections after it require sellers of residential property with one to four units to complete a property condition disclosure form, and section 55-2508 gives the standard form. Describe known problems in plain terms, including anything done without a permit.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Post Falls?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when time or condition is the problem and top price is not. Many Post Falls houses are worth enough that a listing is the better route for a house in good repair, and that is a fair choice.

  • You inherited a house in Kootenai County and live elsewhere.
  • The house needs a roof, a furnace or foundation work that you cannot fund.
  • You are behind on taxes or a mortgage and need to close on a set date.

We buy as-is, and you do not clean, repair or stage. We make an offer after we learn about the house, and you owe nothing if you decline. We do not promise a price before we see the property.

faqs.q: When are Kootenai County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due in full on December 20, under Idaho Code 63-903, and owners of real property may pay in two halves. The second half is due June 20.

faqs.q: What happens if I fall three years behind on Post Falls property taxes?
faqs.a: The parcel enters the tax deed process. The owner must pay the third year delinquency in full to stop it, or the property can be deeded to Kootenai County.

faqs.q: Which school district is Post Falls in?
faqs.a: The city is served by the Post Falls School District 273. Confirm the boundary for your address with the district.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Post Falls house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. We buy houses as-is, so snow damaged roofs, old furnaces and cosmetic wear can stay as they are. You still complete the Idaho property condition disclosure form.

faqs.q: How much snow does Post Falls get?
faqs.a: The yearly average is about 59.3 inches of snow, with December and January the snowiest months. Total precipitation averages about 25.7 inches.
